core_claim.P: The contract owner has explicitly paused the token via the pause mechanism (whenNotPaused enforced on transfer/transferFrom).
core_claim.I: All token movement must cease while paused; batchTransfers and rBatchTransfers should revert when the contract is paused, as transfer and transferFrom do.
core_claim.V: batchTransfers and rBatchTransfers omit the whenNotPaused modifier, so bulk token movements continue even when the contract is paused.

distinct_impacts.description: A compromised or malicious validator can still move tokens via batchTransfers while the contract is paused, bypassing the emergency brake and potentially extracting funds during the window when administrators believe transfers are halted.
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: When the contract is paused, a compromised or malicious validator can still use these functions to move tokens, completely bypassing the emergency brake the protocol owner attempted to engage.

distinct_impacts.description: The pause mechanism, intended as the protocol's last line of defense during security incidents, is defeated because an alternative token-movement pathway remains operational regardless of paused state.
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: The batch transfer functions undermine this expectation entirely, as they provide an alternative pathway for moving tokens that remains operational regardless of the contract's paused state.

distinct_impacts.description: Inconsistency between single-transfer and batch-transfer pause behavior creates confusion about the contract's security guarantees.
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: The inconsistency between single and batch transfer pause behavior also creates confusion about the contract's security guarantees.

distinct_impacts.description: The batch transfer functions lack the whenNotPaused modifier that transfer and transferFrom include, providing an unguarded bulk-movement pathway.
distinct_impacts.evidence_quote: the `batchTransfers` and `rBatchTransfers` functions omit this critical modifier
